subject.title: fix(cron): keep isolated run status ok when delivery fails

question: Should successful isolated cron execution with failed post-run delivery persist as `status=ok` plus `deliveryStatus=not-delivered`, or should this wait for the broader first-class warning-status contract?
rationale: The code path is narrow and tested, but the persisted status, backoff/alert behavior, and external consumer semantics are compatibility-sensitive and require maintainer intent rather than automated repair.

options.title: Approve narrow split
options.body: Land this PR's `ok` plus `not-delivered` behavior and direct consumers to use delivery fields for delivery failures.

options.title: Route through warning status
options.body: Pause this PR and make the broader warning-status model in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/49190 the canonical public contract.

options.title: Keep current error semantics
options.body: Close or defer this fix if delivery-only failures should continue driving `status=error` and error backoff.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow split
recommendation.body: Land this PR's `ok` plus `not-delivered` behavior and direct consumers to use delivery fields for delivery failures.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent broad cron status, trigger, and failure-notification history makes this the strongest available owner for the cross-surface cron status semantics decision.
